chapter: Miles Davis stories and what jazz means
title: Max Roach and the limiting label 'jazz'
summary: They discuss Max Roach's objection to being called a jazz musician and the music's drive for respectability.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience

blocks.x: They say sometimes you have to say, don't bother me I can't cope? (LAUGHTER). I gave up this business of jazz just for the minute though. I like the way you kind of put it in perspective. Max Roach is one of those who is quite oh almost violent now about being described as a jazz musician.
Well you see, it's people who say it in an attempt to demean it.
Yes, and that (it's so limiting limited?). And the connotation of it now, it just seems that it's

Everybody always thinks of jazz in the same way. Practically, even today, people think of it the same way. You can't read, you haven't heard any other music but that, and they have problems trying to accept that. You learn it somewhere where a lot of other low things are happening.
So there's it is an anti-life connotation.
The effort now is really obvious, to make it look white and respectable. (LAUGHTER). Which is to some people, a quite synonymous thing. (LAUGHTER).
